verdicts.quote: A CSV containing one otherwise valid new record and one invalid record creates neither account.
The admin uses the reported reason and location to repair the entry and tries again. … If a reported data-record error concerns a record starting on physical line 5, the error contains the number 5.
A data record whose identity already belongs to a user is a conflict … A repeated identity within a single file is a conflict
An admin cannot assign rights through import that ordinary user creation would prohibit that admin from assigning.
An admin with user-creation authority submits a CSV file through the product. … Import requires admin authority at submission
verdicts.missing: Whether an admin who can create individual users also needs a separate grant to import users in bulk.

verdicts.quote: A file with user values as its first nonempty record and no header is rejected. … A header containing an unrecognized field is rejected. … the import requires an email column … Import uses the ordinary required-field rules
A UTF-8 byte order mark at the beginning of a file is optional … Import accepts both LF and CRLF record endings … Double-quoted CSV fields can contain embedded commas, escaped quotes, or line breaks
If a submission fails in a product that sends onboarding notifications on user creation, its proposed users receive no such notifications from that submission.
A valid file of exactly 1,048,576 bytes passes the byte-size check. A file of 1,048,577 bytes fails it. … A limit rejection tells the admin the maximum for the exceeded measurement.
A zero-byte file, a file containing only empty lines, and a header-only file each fail with an outcome indicating the absence of user records. … A valid one-record submission creates its user.
The admin resubmits a file whose accounts are all still present. No second account is created for any of those identities.
A completed submission has an outcome available to the admin that distinguishes success from failure.
verdicts.missing: Whether large imports run in the background and how the admin finds out when a background import finishes.

verdicts.quote: If ordinary creation requires an onboarding notification for an account in the same state, the imported user receives the corresponding notification after the account is created.
verdicts.missing: Whether a large batch sends all welcome messages at once and, if delivery is paced, what rate or schedule applies.

verdicts.quote: A newly imported user starts in the same initial account state as a comparable ordinarily created user … The imported user follows the product's ordinary account activation or sign-in flow, where one exists.
verdicts.missing: Whether an imported account starts with a password and how the user obtains initial access if the product has no established activation or sign-in flow.

verdicts.quote: If ordinary user creation is required to produce an audit record, a reviewer can find the required audit information for a user created by import.
verdicts.missing: Whether each import must record the importing admin, the affected batch or accounts, and the time of import.

verdicts.missing: Whether the admin can cancel an import in progress and whether the importer offers a retry limited to the rows that reported errors.
